solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Musician's recital isn't bad? About time!

indicators.note: About signals that the shuffled letters go round the letter for time
bad signals that the letters of recital isn't are spoiled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic sighs at a poor recital by a musician: it isn't any good, and it has taken long enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges RECITAL ISN'T into CLARINETIST, and 'About' puts that round T for time. The 's after Musician is a link (is).
explanation.definitionFit: A player of the clarinet is a kind of musician.

clue.text: Everyone turned on tyrant, one from the plains

indicators.note: turned signals that the word for everyone is written backwards

parts.note: everyone means all
Nero was the notoriously tyrannical Roman emperor

explanation.surface: A crowd rounds on a despot, among them a man from the open plains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses the word for everyone; 'on' is only a link. Nero was the Roman emperor famous for cruelty.
explanation.definitionFit: A llanero is a herdsman or cowboy of the South American grassland plains, the llanos.

clue.text: Dragoon fixed radar with oil

indicators.note: fixed suggests repairing, so the letters of radar and oil are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A cavalry soldier repairs a radar set using oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dragoon' looks like a soldier but is the verb: to force someone into something. 'fixed' rearranges RADAR and OIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To dragoon and to railroad both mean to coerce someone into acting, pushing them along without choice.

clue.text: Call for massage on the phone

indicators.note: on the phone means the word is heard spoken rather than seen written

parts.note: to knead is to massage with the hands

explanation.surface: Someone telephones to book a massage.
explanation.definitionFit: To call for something is to require it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: They're poisonous to pandas regularly, more than one saw?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of pandas, the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: a saw is a tool, so several of them are tools

explanation.surface: Something harmful to pandas, perhaps cutting implements?
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes ADS from pandas. 'saw' looks like the past of see but is the cutting implement.
explanation.definitionFit: Many toadstools, the umbrella-shaped fungi, are toxic to eat.

clue.text: Bars to open in fortnight? That's looking up

indicators.note: in a down clue looking up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards
in tells the solver the letters sit inside the word fortnight

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether pubs will open within two weeks, and finds things improving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' takes ORTNI from fortnight and 'looking up' reverses it. 'Bars' are bars of music, not pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: An introduction is the opening passage of a piece of music, its first few bars.

clue.text: Historian understood American

parts.note: tacit means understood without being spoken

explanation.surface: A historian grasped by an American.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus was a celebrated Roman writer of annals and histories of the early empire.

clue.text: Caught up in sense of morality, I promoted lust

indicators.note: in signals that the following pieces are placed inside the reworked word
promoted in a down clue means the letter is moved higher, earlier in the word

parts.note: conscience is one's inner sense of right and wrong
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
taken as written

explanation.surface: A moralist admits that, carried away, lust was put ahead of conscience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoted' moves the I one place earlier, giving CONISCENCE; 'in' then puts the two other pieces inside it after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Concupiscence is a formal word for strong sexual desire.

clue.text: Compassionate description of moth-eaten derelicts?

definitions.meaning: kind and sympathetic, easily moved by others' suffering
worn-out wrecks eaten away by moths are soft and fragile at their core, so whimsically their hearts are tender

explanation.surface: A kindly word for decaying, moth-ridden abandoned things.
explanation.definitionFit: Being soft-hearted and readily feeling pity is to be compassionate.

clue.text: Glass is to give view around a lake

indicators.note: around signals the word for give a view goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to opine is to give one's opinion
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A glass lets one look out over a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaline is a milky, semi-translucent ornamental glass.

clue.text: It could be a tiny portion, with no starter

indicators.note: no starter means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a particle is a minute piece of something

explanation.surface: A dieter wonders whether a tiny bite, without a first course, counts as a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cunning: the little word 'a' is the indefinite article in grammar, so 'It could be a' describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'a' is the indefinite member of this word class, alongside 'the'.

clue.text: Earl tucked into expensive French food

indicators.note: tucked into signals that one letter is placed inside the French word

parts.note: cher is French for expensive

explanation.surface: An aristocrat tucks into costly French cuisine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' looks like eating but means putting E inside CHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheer in an old sense means food and drink, as in good cheer at a feast.

clue.text: Divers when swimming do rest

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: swimming suggests movement, so the letters of do rest are rearranged

explanation.surface: Underwater swimmers take a break between dives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' is not people diving but the old adjective meaning several or various.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers is an archaic word for various or of several kinds, a sense matching a mixed selection.

clue.text: Masculine fellow, one taking role as criminal

parts.note: masculine means male
an actor is someone who takes a role

explanation.surface: A man in a theatre company is cast as a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: A malefactor is a wrongdoer or offender.

clue.text: Support a reptile breeder

parts.note: a prop is a support
gator is a short form of alligator

explanation.surface: Someone backs a person who raises reptiles.
explanation.definitionFit: A propagator raises new plants or stock, breeding and multiplying them.

clue.text: One emperor or another's follower briefly returned

indicators.note: returned signals that the shortened word is read backwards
briefly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a Rasta follows Haile Selassie, another emperor, revered by Rastafarians

explanation.surface: An emperor, or the disciple of a different emperor, made a short return.
explanation.walkthrough: Rastafarians venerate the Ethiopian emperor Haile Selassie, hence 'another's follower'. 'briefly' cuts RASTA to RAST, and 'returned' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was a Russian emperor.

clue.text: Crosses to net reflected inexperienced footballers?

indicators.note: to net is to catch, so the outer word captures the reversed piece

parts.note: fords are crossing points of a river, and to ford is to cross

indicators.note: reflected signals the word is mirrored, read backwards

parts.note: raw means inexperienced, as in a raw recruit

explanation.surface: Crosses into goal from untried footballers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' reverses the word for inexperienced and 'to net' traps it. The question mark flags a definition by example: forwards are only some footballers.
explanation.definitionFit: Forwards are the attacking players in a football team.

clue.text: Indian spinach has zero starch

parts.note: sag is spinach in Indian cooking, as in sag aloo
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A dish of Indian spinach contains no starch.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is a starch extracted from palm pith, used in puddings.

clue.text: Be unused and become furious

definitions.meaning: to be left over or spare, not taken up
British slang for getting very angry

explanation.surface: Something left idle drives its owner mad.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase has two senses: to remain available and unused, and in British slang to lose one's temper.

clue.text: Redistribute troubled locale's housing cost? On the contrary

indicators.note: housing signals that one piece contains another
On the contrary reverses the roles, so the cost word holds the other piece instead

parts.note: a rate is a cost or charge

indicators.note: troubled signals that the letters of locale are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Shift around the housing costs of a troubled area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' makes EALLOC. Read straight, 'housing' would put the cost inside the anagram; 'On the contrary' flips that, so the cost holds it.
explanation.definitionFit: To reallocate is to share out again, assigning resources differently.

clue.text: Content to land good fish, doing this?

definitions.text: Content to land good fish, doing this?

indicators.note: content means what is inside, so the middle letters of land are taken

parts.note: ling is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone happy just to catch a decent fish, which is what this activity is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like happy but here means the inside, AN from land. The whole clue describes the pastime too.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishing with rod and line, hoping to land a good one, is exactly this sport.

clue.text: Mug shot a suspect finally may see

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken, so the letters are rearranged
finally takes the last letter of suspect

explanation.surface: A police mug shot that a suspect might eventually get to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' is not a face but a gullible person. 'shot' rearranges A MAY SEE into EASYMEA, and 'finally' adds the last letter of suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: A mug is a dupe; an easy target is someone simple to fool or beat.

clue.text: Tooth damage has initially occasioned large filling

indicators.note: filling signals that the picked letters go inside the word for damage

parts.note: to mar is to damage

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of occasioned and large

explanation.surface: A dentist notes tooth damage that first required a big filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling' looks dental but puts O and L inside MAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A molar is a back grinding tooth.

clue.text: Name-dropping scorer is to make bet

indicators.note: dropping signals the letter is left out of the composer's name

parts.note: a scorer is a composer of musical scores; Wagner is one

explanation.surface: A footballer who namedrops is about to place a bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scorer' suggests a goalscorer, but it is a composer of scores: Wagner.
explanation.definitionFit: To wager is to stake money on an outcome, to gamble.

clue.text: One secures right to get some land

indicators.note: secures means holds firmly, so the word for one contains the letter

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: Someone obtains the right to acquire a plot.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land area, a measured plot.

clue.text: Wreath quietly placed in holiday home

indicators.note: placed in signals the letter goes inside the word for the holiday home

parts.note: a chalet is a holiday cabin
P stands for piano, quietly in music

explanation.surface: A garland is quietly hung in a holiday cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplet is a garland or circlet of flowers for the head.

clue.text: Blimey! Delightful architectural feature!

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like blimey
nice means delightful

explanation.surface: A visitor exclaims at a lovely piece of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornice is a decorative moulding running along the top of a wall or building.

clue.text: Windows may show one splashed some grease around car

indicators.note: around signals the shuffled letters go round the car abbreviation
splashed suggests scattering, so the letters of some grease are rearranged

parts.note: RR, Rolls-Royce, stands for a car

explanation.surface: A mechanic splashes grease over a car, and its windows show it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Windows' is the Microsoft operating system, not a car's glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer program displays an alert box when something fails, warning the user of a fault.
